scope: 2014-10 survey exterior of police office with directly connected residence A and later additions; report issued 2015-06.
method: Independent inspection of all nine normalized preview images, cross-checked against derived source controls and the independent 44-check mesh/CSG report.

views.observation: Complete combined phase massing and open tall frame; timber end board triangle exposed.
Stepped residence roof and two rear host planes closed; red gable faces visible.
Entire base and roof footprint visible; stepped rear roof and low corridor retained.
Front crest, three entry steps, recessed entrance and two timber windows visible; no restored historical emblem.
Stepped brick gable and unequal lower/upper RC rear windows retained.
Timber gable board joints visibly exposed below thin roof shell; low corridor and two-storey RC phase visible.
Original office and residence side openings not blocked by plinth belt; stepped rear return closed.
Intentional detail crop; red lamp and neutral foliage proxy, entry bands and exposed openings inspected.
Intentional detail crop; brick gable outside roof, closed notch return and opaque service portal inspected.

resolved_geometry_issues: Residence rear brick gable faces extend beyond roof ends rather than being swallowed.
Timber roof is a thin shell; actual final-mesh cream triangular wall and contrasting weatherboard joints are exposed.
Door-crossing plinth belts removed and unsupported timber transoms omitted.
limitations: Neighbor-obscured fine finish is not fully reconstructed; source-supported openings are distinguished from neutral unknown plates.
Graphically estimated dimensions and engineering offsets are disclosed, not claimed as survey-grade coordinates.
Opaque glazing, simplified foliage/red lamp and generic roof texture are model proxies.
No interior reconstruction, structural certification or physical test print.
